title: Mapping Stakeholders to Drive Alignment
description: Learn to map stakeholders by power and interest so you can prioritize who to align first.

interactions.prompt: Which quadrant should receive the MOST engagement effort?

options.text: High power, high interest
High power, low interest
Low power, high interest
Low power, low interest

interactions.teachingPreamble: A Power-Interest Matrix is a 2×2 grid that plots stakeholders by their authority (power) and their engagement level (interest) in your project. At Spotify, product managers use this matrix before every major launch to decide who needs a deep briefing versus a simple update. The goal is to focus your limited time on stakeholders who can make or break your initiative.

interactions.prompt: A project lead at Shopify logged stakeholder interactions: CFO (2 meetings, blocked budget twice), Head of Design (8 meetings, no decision authority), VP Engineering (1 email, approved all past roadmaps). Who is the most under-engaged high-power stakeholder?

options.text: CFO — high interaction already, just disagreeing
Head of Design — most meetings means most important
VP Engineering — approval power but barely contacted
All three are equally engaged

interactions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of identifying a stakeholder's underlying interest?

options.text: To manipulate them into agreement
To find common ground and reduce conflicts
To document their weaknesses for leverage
To assign them less important tasks

interactions.teachingPreamble: Stakeholder conflicts often arise not from opposing goals but from different underlying interests. When Airbnb's trust & safety team clashed with growth teams over verification requirements, a facilitator discovered both cared about long-term retention — they just defined it differently. Mapping what stakeholders truly care about (not just what they say) lets you find alignment opportunities.

interactions.prompt: In stakeholder mapping, you should 'manage closely' those with high ____ and high interest, while simply 'monitoring' those low in both.

options.text: Salary
Power
Seniority
Availability

interactions.prompt: You're launching a new CRM integration at HubSpot. The VP of Sales (high power) wants a quick rollout by Q2. The IT Security lead (high power) demands a 3-month audit first. You can't do both on time. What's your best move?

options.text: Side with VP Sales — revenue always wins
Side with IT Security — compliance is non-negotiable
Propose a phased rollout: limited launch with parallel security audit
Escalate to CEO and let them decide

interactions.prompt: Why should you engage 'keep satisfied' stakeholders (high power, low interest) differently from 'manage closely' ones?

options.text: They need frequent detailed updates to stay engaged
They can block you if surprised, but don't want heavy involvement
They have no real influence on outcomes
They should be treated exactly the same way

interactions.teachingPreamble: Not every powerful stakeholder wants to be in every meeting. At Microsoft, when the Azure team launched a new pricing model, the CFO had veto power but no desire to attend weekly standups. The team sent concise monthly briefs instead. Over-engaging these stakeholders wastes their time and yours; under-engaging them risks a late-stage veto that derails everything.

interactions.prompt: You're a PM at Stripe prioritizing stakeholder alignment for a new fraud detection feature. Rank these stakeholders from FIRST to engage to LAST: (a) Legal team — high power, low interest, slow to respond; (b) CEO — high power, high interest, quarterly check-in scheduled; (c) Merchant support team — low power, high interest, vocal advocates; (d) External payment partner — low power, low interest, contractual dependency only.

options.text: Legal — high power, low interest, slow responder
CEO — high power, high interest
Merchant support — low power, high interest
External partner — low power, low interest

interactions.prompt: Midway through your Stripe fraud feature, the external payment partner announces they're building a competing fraud tool and threatens to end the partnership. How do you reprioritize?

options.text: Ignore them — they were low priority on your map
Immediately elevate the partner to 'manage closely' and schedule alignment talks
Ask the merchant support team to handle the relationship
Cancel your fraud feature to avoid conflict

interactions.priorContext: Previously the external payment partner was mapped as low power, low interest. Now they've announced a competing product and threatened the partnership, dramatically shifting their power and interest levels on your stakeholder map.
